m1-t1.introduction: A second way to understand “From HR activity to a decision question”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Start with the decision, not the chart
sections.explanation: A useful HR question connects a defined population and period to an action someone is authorised to consider.

items.label: Decision owner
items.detail: Name who needs to decide and what authority they have.

items.label: Question and boundary
items.detail: Specify the population, period and operational concern.

items.label: Relevant evidence
items.detail: Choose data that can answer that question safely.

items.label: Proportionate action
items.detail: Recommend a next check or bounded process change.

sections.takeaway: A count of activity does not prove that the activity improved hiring or workforce outcomes.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Start with the decision and stakeholder

sections.title: Four analysis types are different questions
sections.explanation: Description, diagnosis, prediction and action evaluation are not a mandatory maturity ladder. A careful count may be enough.

items.label: Describe
items.detail: What happened under an explicit counting rule?

items.label: Investigate
items.detail: Which explanations should be checked next?

items.label: Predict
items.detail: What might occur under stated modelling assumptions?

items.label: Evaluate action
items.detail: Which options deserve an authorised, proportionate test?

sections.takeaway: An association is not a cause, and a prediction is not permission for an employment decision.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Define what one row and one count mean
sections.explanation: An application, a person, a requisition and an employment event are different analytical units.

items.label: Name the grain
items.detail: State what one record represents.

items.label: Choose the key
items.detail: Identify the field or combination that should be unique.

items.label: Set inclusion rules
items.detail: Declare periods, statuses and exclusions.

items.label: Record a dictionary
items.detail: Make the definition reproducible for another analyst.

sections.takeaway: Keep the definition stable during a comparison rather than changing it to improve the result.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Does a higher interview count prove that hiring improved?
checkpoint.answer: No. It describes activity under a counting rule. The decision needs suitable outcome evidence, a defined population and context.

m1-t2.introduction: A second way to understand “Employee lifecycle and a useful metric dictionary”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Follow the event and the responsible owner
sections.explanation: A candidate moves through distinct lifecycle events. Acceptance, joining, development and exit are not interchangeable states.

items.label: Plan and attract
items.detail: Define the approved need and the recruitment owner.

items.label: Select and offer
items.detail: Use job-related evidence and record the actual decision events.

items.label: Join and develop
items.detail: Confirm entry, onboarding and later changes with the relevant owner.

items.label: Move or exit
items.detail: Record effective dates and distinguish transfers from organisation exits.

sections.takeaway: Do not count an accepted offer as a confirmed join or a payroll row as proof of active employment.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A metric dictionary is an agreement about meaning
sections.explanation: The label on a dashboard must connect to an inspectable formula, source and business use.

items.label: Question
items.detail: Which decision will the metric support?

items.label: Formula
items.detail: What are the numerator and eligible denominator?

items.label: Boundary
items.detail: Which period, population and exclusions apply?

items.label: Source and owner
items.detail: Who maintains the input and definition?

items.label: Limitations
items.detail: What would make the result incomplete or misleading?

sections.takeaway: Do not average metrics whose populations or time conventions are incompatible.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 2. Build a metric dictionary before a dashboard

sections.title: A stock is a state; a flow is an event count
sections.explanation: Snapshots and interval events reconcile only when dates, population and movement rules agree.

items.label: Snapshot
items.detail: Count active people at a stated point in time.

items.label: Period flow
items.detail: Count included joins, exits and movements during an interval.

items.label: Boundary check
items.detail: Apply the correct organisation or department rules before reconciling.

sections.takeaway: Internal transfers cancel at organisation level but change department totals.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 3. Snapshots and flows answer different questions

checkpoint.question: Should a transfer between two departments reduce total organisation headcount?
checkpoint.answer: Not if the person remains in the organisation under the same counting scope. It changes department movements, which must be reconciled separately.

m1-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Privacy, access and safe people-data practice”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: A field needs a purpose before it needs a formula
sections.explanation: Minimising data reduces exposure and often makes the analysis clearer. The course uses synthetic records, not real employee data.

items.label: Define the question
items.detail: Identify the minimum evidence needed.

items.label: Remove unnecessary fields
items.detail: Prefer aggregates or synthetic examples for practice.

items.label: Confirm access
items.detail: Use authorised storage, processing and recipients.

items.label: Review sharing
items.detail: Send only the layer the recipient actually needs.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload identifiable candidate or employee records to public AI tools or personal accounts.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Replacing a name does not guarantee anonymity
sections.explanation: A re-identification key, a rare role or a combination of filters can reveal a person behind a pseudonym.

items.label: Direct key
items.detail: An ID can still link to an identifiable source.

items.label: Rare combination
items.detail: Role, location and tenure may narrow to one person.

items.label: Small cell
items.detail: A tiny group can reveal individual outcomes.

items.label: Complementary inference
items.detail: Totals or adjacent views can expose a suppressed value.

sections.takeaway: Review indirect disclosure and complementary totals; a classroom small-cell threshold is not a legal anonymity guarantee.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Governance is more than a checkbox
sections.explanation: Purpose, authority, access, retention and remedies must match the actual processing arrangement.

items.label: Establish authority
items.detail: Confirm the permitted purpose and applicable process.

items.label: Apply safeguards
items.detail: Limit fields, access and retention appropriately.

items.label: Support review
items.detail: Provide the required correction, concern and rights routes.

items.label: Check the actual workflow
items.detail: Verify controls and update them when the use changes.

sections.takeaway: Check current official requirements through qualified institutional owners; a classroom diagram is not legal advice.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 3. Governance is broader than a consent checkbox

checkpoint.question: If names are replaced with IDs, is a workforce spreadsheet automatically anonymous?
checkpoint.answer: No. IDs, rare combinations, small groups and totals can still enable re-identification. Review the actual sharing and disclosure risks.
